subject.summary: An eight-note child's toy xylophone: eight lacquered metal bars in rainbow colours, longest to shortest, pegged over felt pads on a painted wooden trapezoid frame, with two beech mallets lying in front.

facts.value: eight metal bars, longest to shortest, in rainbow colours
each bar resting on felt pads
each bar held by two small rubber pegs
two beech mallets with round red rubber heads, lying in front

facts.note: a typical toy xylophone bar; the octave taper fixes the shortest
0.708 of the longest, the octave ratio of a free-free bar
spring steel / aluminium bar stock of this size
trapezoid plan, measured at the bass end

parts.label: Wide end of the frame (bass end)
Narrow end of the frame (treble end)

next: bevel the bars' top edges for a softer highlight
give the frame a real hole-and-bead so a bar can be swapped
round the frame's four vertical corners
